title: Avimi bar Pappi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the colleague of Rav Nachman and Ulla, as in [Ketubot 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.53a.13) and Avodah Zarah 53b: “Rav Nachman, Ulla and Avimi bar Pappi were sitting, and Rav Chiyya bar Ami was sitting with them.” And as in [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.4.13.2): “Rabbi Zeira asked Rav Nachman bar Yaakov and Rabbi Avimi bar Pappi”; there in [6:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.6.6.3) the reading is Rabbi Ami bar Pappi, which Hyman identifies as the same person. In Ketubot 43a Avimi bar Pappi said to Rabbi Zeira: “Shakur said it.” Hyman finds the parallel in [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.4.2.3) and cites 4:13 as well: “Rabbi Zeira sent to Rav Nachman bar Yaakov and to Rabbi Imi bar Pappi — he said to him: Shakur said it.”[^3]

notes.text: The supplied Shakur is retained alongside saved Davidson Ketubot 43b’s Shakud and Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:2’s Shoked, identified there as Shmuel. The supplied 43a locator remains rather than being erased. Hyman’s Ami/Avimi/Imi identification is attributed, not imposed on authorities.

The inspected Ketubot 43b has Avimi bar Pappi saying Shakud said it and identifies Shakud as Shmuel. The inspected Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:2 has Imi bar Pappi and Shoked. Hyman’s supplied Shakur, 43a locator and Ami/Avimi/Imi equation remain visible as his readings and identification.

The parallel in [Ketubot 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.43b.1-2) has Avimi credit Shakud, whom the passage identifies as Shmuel. The Gemara clarifies that Shmuel also gave the teaching, since Rav has already been credited. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=152&lang=en) cites 43b, gives Avodah Zarah 63b rather than 53b, and treats Imi as a scribal error. In the linked Yerushalmi, 4:2 concerns the daughter’s earnings and reads Imi. The linked 4:13 question concerns housing and reads Avimi, while 6:6 reads Ami.
